publication_status.evidence: As for 9 Sgr (eso-9sgr.json): Crossref and the VizieR ReadMe. Element values are read from the Fig. A.9 panel of the arXiv PDF. The paper calls this a preliminary orbit.

method: As for 9 Sgr. The SB2 radial velocities were ignored in the fit (Sect. 3.9): the radial-velocity elements are degenerate and the individual masses unconstrained.
flux_ratio_definition: f_H = secondary / primary in the H band, 0.77 +/- 0.02 (Fig. A.9 panel), constant over epochs.
uncertainties: As for 9 Sgr. The orbit is badly constrained: a = 7.0 +/- 3.9 mas, e = 0.902 +/- 0.058 with a strong a-e-omega degeneracy (the scatterplots of Fig. A.9), and the periastron lies in a gap, so the paper's own 'preliminary' applies. Le Bouquin+17 (Table B.1 caption, CDS ReadMe note 3) calls emax/emin the FWHM of the error ellipse's axes; Fabry+21 (Table A.2 caption) calls the same numbers 1-sigma. They cannot both be right: the factor is 2 sqrt(2 ln 2) = 2.3548. Stored as published; do not convert before the first blind fit shows which reading gives pulls of order 1.

conventions.omega: the secondary's, from the ascending node (Sect. 2.4); omega_shift_deg = 0 is taken from the paper's text, not checked (see eso-9sgr). The RVs were ignored in this fit, so the published (omega, Omega) = (246.7, 231.2) deg is one arbitrary half of the pair: (66.7, 51.2) deg gives the same positions and is equally correct. crosscheck.orbits with the published T reproduces the 11 published epochs to 0.30 mas rms (worst 0.68 mas at the epoch with a 24 mas ellipse); that checks the transcription, not the node. Compare omega and Omega modulo the joint 180 deg flip.
conventions.inclination: i = 105.2 deg > 90: clockwise on the sky, PA decreasing in time
conventions.T: T = 53525 +/- 14 MJD, a periastron 0.78 P before the first epoch (MJD 54964); only T modulo P matters

error_ellipse_published.convention: FWHM per Le Bouquin+17, 1-sigma per Fabry+21: see conventions.uncertainties

other.note: rho and PA are the best-fit two-point-star position of the secondary relative to the primary; no rho/PA errors are tabulated, only the error ellipse
